Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image depict the source image as a drawing made from chalk?
node.criteria: Compare SOURCE and EDITED across the scene, including salient subjects and background. Assess whether the source content is actually rendered in a chalk-drawing visual form, not merely softened or covered by grain, smudging, or chalk-like texture. A scene-wide chalk-made rendering is complete. A mixed rendering is partial when substantial salient content still reads as photographic, even if other regions have a concrete chalk-drawing appearance. Residual detail alone does not make an otherwise genuinely chalk-made drawing incomplete.
node.binding: SOURCE is the image to transform; EDITED must show that same image rendered as a chalk drawing. Compare the rendering of salient depicted content as well as the overall scene; texture or treatment alone is not sufficient evidence of a chalk-made rendering.
node.source_quote: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
node.endpoint: The source image is rendered as a chalk-made drawing.
node.necessity: This is the requested transformation itself; without it, the instruction is not fulfilled.
node.zero_when: The edited image shows no requested chalk-drawing transformation of the source image; unrelated edits or a chalk-like texture or overlay without chalk rendering of depicted content do not count.
node.half_when: The source image has a concrete chalk-drawing appearance in some regions, but substantial salient content still reads as photographic or retains photographic structure, leaving the scene mixed rather than genuinely reading overall as a chalk-made drawing. Do not treat residual detail alone as incomplete when the scene genuinely reads as chalk-made.
node.full_when: The edited image presents the source image’s salient depicted content across the scene as a drawing made from chalk, so the scene genuinely reads as chalk-made rather than merely softened, textured, or overlaid. Natural variation in lighting, texture, and detail is allowed; residual photographic detail alone does not prevent full achievement when the rendering as a whole is genuinely chalk-made.

node_traces.evidence: The two giraffes and surrounding scene have been substantially re-rendered with soft, grainy, chalk-like shading and drawn outlines, so this is more than a simple texture overlay. However, the giraffes retain fairly photographic anatomy and coat detail, while the background is heavily blurred and smudged rather than clearly rendered as chalk. The scene has a partial chalk-drawing appearance but does not consistently read as a chalk-made drawing across salient content.
